Flood Insurance Data

About Flood Insurance Data

What this is

Flood Insurance Data is an independent project that makes the U.S. government's own flood-insurance records readable one place at a time. For each county we publish what existing NFIP policyholders actually pay, how that compares with FEMA's full-risk price, the claims history, the flood risk, and the community discounts that lower the bill — every figure drawn from a public federal dataset, with its exact source and the date it was pulled.

How the numbers are made and checked

  • Compiled directly from FEMA's OpenFEMA records and FEMA's National Risk Index; no private data. One figure is a FEMA model and is labeled as such: the National Risk Index.
  • Every page is built by code and ships only after an automated correctness gate passes it: percentiles and sums are recomputed, record counts are checked against the download's own totals (FEMA's separate official policy count is not yet compared), every ratio's denominator is disclosed, and nothing publishes if a check fails. The methodology defines every term.
  • We show aggregates only — never an individual property, policy, or quote.
  • Corrections & contact: contact@floodinsurancedata.com — tell us about any figure that looks wrong and we will check it against the source record.

Independence

This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by FEMA or any government agency, and has no relationship with any insurer, agent, or lead-generation service. It does not sell insurance, generate quotes, or earn commissions on policies. It is a reference, not a sales page. The site shows ads served by Google AdSense (see the privacy page); ads never change a figure, and no advertiser has a say in what is published.

The site is run anonymously, by choice: there is no named author. Every figure instead names its exact federal source and date, and the methodology shows how each one is counted, so a reader can check it.

This product uses FEMA's OpenFEMA API but is not endorsed by FEMA. Place names via GeoNames (CC BY 4.0). Aggregates only, never individual quotes. About · Methodology · Data · Privacy · Terms
